message.content: In lions, the most well‑known dominant genetic trait is the **presence of a mane in males**. The mane is largely controlled by the androgen receptor (AR) gene, which is inherited in a dominant fashion. Male lions inherit one copy of the AR allele that promotes mane development; if they receive a functional allele from either parent, they will develop a mane (though its size and coloration can vary). This dominant trait is why all male lions typically have some mane, whereas females do not.
